title: The Extraction of the Free Port
premise: Ansel Almeida, a whistle-blower living under four names, is approached by a stranger named Iva who claims Ansel once saved her life — a favor he has no memory of, and which may never have happened. The debt she invokes pulls him into a plot to destroy the Free Port, a bonded warehouse city where the world's elites hide assets and secrets; the attack is scheduled to look like an industrial accident. As Ansel and Iva race to expose the operation before it burns, he discovers his own fabricated identities were built by the same network that plans the attack, making him both witness and intended scapegoat. In the end, Ansel chooses truth over survival, sacrificing his last alias to broadcast the evidence, while Iva — whose 'favor' was a manufactured memory designed to recruit him — breaks from her handlers and becomes the one real thing in his life.
about_author: Lena Voss spent a decade as an investigative researcher in European logistics hubs before turning to fiction, drawing on the shadow economies of bonded warehouses and flag-of-convenience shipping. She writes under a pen name and lives, like her protagonists, somewhere between four addresses.

chapters.title: The Man with Four Names
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. We meet him mid-case in Rotterdam, ghosting through the Free Port's corridors under his third identity this year, documenting what the warehouses hide. A near-miss with port security shows how thin his margins are. Emotional beat: competent loneliness — a man so practiced at vanishing that no one would notice if he did.

chapters.title: A Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: Iva finds Ansel in Lisbon, repaying a debt for a rescue he cannot remember — cash, documents, and a warning that someone is buying explosives-grade chemicals through Free Port channels. He refuses; she leaves a ledger page anyway. Emotional beat: unease — the kindness feels engineered, and Ansel can't stop turning it over.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: Iva's POV. She reports to her handler that the hook is set, revealing fragments of her mission: Ansel was chosen, cultivated, and the 'favor' was implanted via a staged incident years ago. But reviewing the file, she notices anomalies suggesting her own memories were edited too. Emotional beat: first hairline crack in her certainty.

chapters.title: The Ledger Page
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Following the ledger, he confirms a shipment of thermite precursors routed through shell companies tied to the Free Port's own audit firm. When he tries to pass the finding to an old journalist contact, the contact is already dead — ruled accidental. Emotional beat: dread hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Two Liars, One Room
chapters.summary: Iva's POV. Ordered to keep Ansel on track, she engineers a second meeting, but he confronts her with proof the favor was staged. Cornered, she gives him a half-truth: the attack is real, scheduled within weeks, meant to erase records and bodies alike. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance between two people who know they're being played.

chapters.title: The Accident Calendar
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The pair traces the attack plan: a fire timed to coincide with a safety inspection, blaming a dead contractor — a profile that matches, exactly, one of Ansel's discarded aliases. They realize he isn't just a witness; he's the designated culprit. Emotional beat: betrayal curdling into urgency.

chapters.title: What the Port Keeps
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Inside the deepest vaults, they find the true target: not contraband but the network's own archive of blackmail — including files on Iva's handlers and a dossier on Ansel's original self, the name he lost. Emotional beat: vertigo of identity — the man he was is a weapon aimed at the man he became.

chapters.title: Handlers
chapters.summary: Iva's POV. Her handler activates the endgame, ordering her to deliver Ansel to the site before detonation. Instead she feeds the network false coordinates, burning her cover irreversibly. A brutal confrontation with a fellow operative ends with her wounded and committed. Emotional beat: the found-family choice — choosing Ansel over the only structure she's ever known.

chapters.title: Detonation Day
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating POV. At the Free Port, Ansel triggers the sprinkler-flood failsafe and hijacks the port's internal broadcast to stream the archive while Iva holds off the strike team among the container stacks. The explosion happens — smaller, contained, blamed on them. Emotional beat: terror, sacrifice, and the strange calm of finally standing visibly in the open.

chapters.title: One Name Left
chapters.summary: Resolution, Ansel's POV. The broadcast forces inquiries; three governments disown the network, and Ansel's four names are all burned — but the archive restored his original identity, and he claims it publicly, testimony attached. Recovering, Iva asks who he'll be now. He answers: someone who stays. Emotional beat: quiet rebirth — loyalty chosen over safety, truth over survival.
